subject: SLA negotiation: uptime baseline, monthly credits, and maintenance exception path
messages:
From: Marcus Rivera <marcus.rivera@cloudline.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline and maintenance carveout question

Rachel —

Thanks for the run-through last week. Before our procurement committee meets next Tuesday we need a concise summary of the uptime/latency commitments and the exception path you typically accept for scheduled maintenance tied to major model upgrades. Two specific asks from our side:

- Confirm Redwood's standard hosted uptime percentage for production clusters in us-west and any region-specific deviations.
- Explain how monthly service credits would be calculated if we see sustained degradation during a model rollout (we're worried about rollouts that last several hours). Also, do you offer a grace allowance for short, non-customer-impacting degradations?

High level constraints from Cloudline: we need either a 99.95% uptime target or a transparent credit schedule that scales predictably; we prefer a fixed cap on credits (so finance can model exposure). Can you also confirm whether maintenance windows (if communicated 7+ days in advance) are excluded from uptime calculations?

If helpful, attach your standard SLA template and any worked examples for monthly credit calculation.

Appreciate a short reply — Marcus

--
Marcus Rivera
Director, Ops & Platform
Cloudline AI
marcus.rivera@cloudline.ai
+1 415-555-0199

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Rivera <marcus.rivera@cloudline.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and maintenance carveout question

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: our standard hosted uptime target is 99.95% for US regions, and the default monthly credit schedule is proportional to minutes of unavailability with a predictable cap tied to monthly committed spend. Maintenance windows that are scheduled and communicated at least 72 hours in advance are generally excluded; longer planned upgrades that require rolling restarts are handled case-by-case.

I've looped in Karthik (sales) and Laura (legal) to propose concrete language and a worked example. Attached: the SLA_v3_proposed.pdf which shows the standard baseline plus two optional exception paths we typically offer to enterprise customers.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to provide a redline option that preserves a capped financial exposure for Redwood while giving Cloudline a predictable credit formula.
- Karthik to confirm whether Cloudline expects a hard dollar cap or a percentage-of-invoice cap.
- Marcus to confirm if a 72-hour advance notice for planned model upgrades is acceptable for your operations team (you asked about 7+ days; we can accommodate that if you prefer).

If we can agree on the cap approach today, I can prep a DocuSign envelope with the redlined SLA for signature.

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and maintenance carveout question

Rachel / Karthik —

Draft redlines below. High-level goal: keep Redwood's maximum exposure predictable while offering Cloudline a deterministic credit model they can budget against. Key points I'm proposing:

1) Uptime baseline
- Keep 99.95% as the standard uptime target for production in us regions.

2) Monthly credit calculation (alternative approach)
- Introduce a "graceband": the first 30 minutes of aggregated unavailability in any calendar month are excluded from credit calculations per production cluster. This accounts for short transient events and rollout noise.
- After the graceband, credits are calculated in 30-minute blocks as: (Monthly committed fees / 720) * block_count * credit_factor. Credit_factor is 0.25 for each 30-minute block for partial availability; if a block meets the definition of outage (no successful API responses for the region), credit_factor is 1.0.
- Example: $120,000 monthly commit → per-block value = $120,000 / 720 = $166.67. A single outage block (30m) = $166.67 credit; three outage blocks = $500.01.

3) Cap on credits
- Offer two cap options for negotiation: (A) fixed dollar cap equal to 50% of monthly committed fees, or (B) fixed dollar cap of $250,000, whichever is lower. This allows predictable exposure for Redwood while giving Cloudline downside protection.

4) Planned maintenance carveout
- Maintenance outage windows that are communicated at least 7 days in advance and scheduled during agreed maintenance windows (by default Sundays 02:00–06:00 PT) are excluded. Emergency maintenance is treated per incident classification and can be excluded if caused by Cloudline configuration.

5) Rollout exception path
- For major model upgrades expected to exceed 2 hours of aggregate cluster restarts, parties agree to a "rollout plan" (email + ops playbook) 14 days in advance. If a rollout plan is provided, the graceband doubles (60 minutes) for the rollout window only; credits are calculated after the doubled graceband.

I attach my redlined comments in redlines_SLA_v3_comments.docx. If Karthik confirms Cloudline prefers option A or B for the cap, I can prepare final language to insert into section 5.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & Legal
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: redlines_SLA_v3_comments.docx (12KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and maintenance carveout question

Marcus —

Thanks again for the quick turnaround. Laura and Karthik and I aligned on language that I think meets Cloudline's need for predictability while keeping exposure bounded for Redwood. Summary of agreed proposal below — if this matches what you expect, I'll send a DocuSign with the two agreed edits (graceband + cap option) and an attached worked example for your finance team.

Agreed summary:
- Baseline uptime: 99.95% for production clusters in us-west (applies to other regions by written amendment).
- Graceband: first 30 minutes of aggregated unavailability excluded per month per cluster.
- Credit calculation: post-graceband, credits measured in 30-minute blocks; per-block value = committed_monthly_fees / 720; credit factor = 1.0 for full outage blocks; 0.25 for partial-degradation blocks.
- Cap: Cloudline to choose one at signature: (A) cap = 50% of monthly committed fees OR (B) cap = $250,000 (whichever is lower).
- Maintenance: planned maintenance communicated >= 7 days in advance and scheduled in agreed windows is excluded.
- Rollouts: for major upgrades with a 14-day plan, graceband doubles to 60 minutes for the rollout window only.

Next actions: please reply with which cap you prefer (Option A or B) and whether you want the 7-day or 72-hour notice threshold for routine maintenance. Once you confirm, I'll prepare the DocuSign link and include the SLA_v3_proposed.pdf + our redlines.
